title: Isolation levels: what can B see of A?
intro: Txn A changes a balance but has not committed. Should Txn B be allowed to see that unsaved number?

predict.question: At READ UNCOMMITTED, B reads Alice's balance while A has an unsaved change to 0. Then A rolls back. What does B see?
predict.reveal: B reads the dirty value 0. A rolled back, so 0 was never real. Higher isolation levels stop B from seeing it.

takeaway: Higher isolation hides more of other transactions' work: READ COMMITTED stops dirty reads, REPEATABLE READ also keeps your reads stable.

steps.say: Alice's balance is 100. Two transactions are about to use it at the same time.
Txn A starts a withdrawal and sets the balance to 0. It has NOT committed yet, so this might still be undone.
Txn B reads the balance. It runs at the weakest level, READ UNCOMMITTED, which lets it see unsaved changes.
The database hands B the value 0. B just read data that nobody has committed. This is a dirty read.
Now Txn A changes its mind and rolls back. The balance returns to 100.
B is holding a 0 that never really existed. It may have refused a purchase or shown a wrong total. That is the danger.
Replay at a higher level. A again sets the balance to 0 without committing. B now runs at READ COMMITTED.
B reads again. The database only shows data that has been committed.
B gets 100, the last committed value. A's unsaved 0 stays hidden. The dirty read is gone.
Now A commits, so 0 is the real balance.
B reads again in the same transaction. At READ COMMITTED it now sees 0, so one query gave 100 and the next gave 0. That is a non-repeatable read.
REPEATABLE READ would give B a stable snapshot, 100 both times, until B finishes. Stronger isolation, fewer surprises.
